newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end up, soyoil rally boosts late.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end up, soyoil rally boosts late.

text.p: Soybean futures on the Chicago Board of Trade ended modestly higher Thursday on strength borrowed from a late rally in soyoil futures, CBOT traders said.
"The (soy)oil started rallying and the beans just took off," said one floor trader.
Trade had been choppy but firm as traders struggled to interpret weather news from Brazil, floor sources said.
Most of the major soybean growing states in Brazil received rain overnight, but bulls said it wasn't enough to reverse all crop concerns, traders said.

Scattered showers of .10 to .50 inch were reported in the major soybean areas of Rio Grande Do Sul and southwest Parana, but some clearing was expected over the next few days, according to Weather Services Corp.
Weekly USDA export sales of 81,600 tonnes were well below trade estimates and conidered bearish to Thursday's trade, floor sources said.
CBOT soybean futures ended 1/4 to 5-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with January up 1/4 at $6.95-3/4 and March up 3-1/4 cents at $6.99-1/4.
Some said the market's strength was linked to speculator anticipation of a cut in the soybean carry-out in the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Supply and Demand Report on Friday.
The trade average for final 1996 soybean production was 2.407 billion bushels from a range of 2.315 to 2.454 billion. USDA's last estimate was 2.403 billion bushels.

On the day, Prudential Securities bought two billion bushels March, Merrill Lynch bought one million March and FIMAT Futures bought 1.5 million March. Cargill Investor Service sold 1.5 million May and Smith Barney sold one million March.
In options trading, L.B. Stern bought 200 May $9.00 calls, Refco sold 250 March $7.50 calls and Continental Grain sold 250 March $7.25 calls, traders said.
Soybean volume was estimated at 30,000 contracts, slightly below the 30,980 contracts traded on Wednesday, according to CBOT data.
